title: Sunscreen-Flavored Ice Cream? Van Leeuwen CEO to Revisit Korea in October
snippet: Van Leeuwen CEO Ben Van Leeuwen will revisit Korea in October to advance plans for a "Flavor Lab" store, as premium ice cream competition intensifies among
extractedText: Sunscreen-Flavored Ice Cream? Van Leeuwen CEO to Revisit Korea in OctoberNew York Ice Cream Brand Van Leeuwen Enters Korea Push to Introduce 'Flavor Lab' Store Specialized in New Product Development From Benson to Terarosa: Premium Ice Cream Competition Heats UpFinance|Published 2026.07.05. 11:00:05|By Noh Hyun-young|Summary|SaveAAABen Vanrooijen, CEO, speaks at a press conference marking the opening of the company's first domestic store, held at the Vanrooijen Gangnam Station branch in Gangnam-gu, Seoul, on the 2nd. Photo courtesy of A Twosome PlaceBen Van Leeuwen, co-founder and chief executive of U.S. premium ice cream brand Van Leeuwen, will visit Korea again this October. The trip will come about three months after his visit earlier this month for the opening of the brand's first Korean store at Gangnam Station on the 3rd. The move is seen as an effort to solidify plans to introduce the "Flavor Lab," a store specialized in new product development that the company operates in the United States.According to industry sources, CEO Van Leeuwen will visit Korea in October to discuss the Flavor Lab operation plans with A Twosome Place. The Flavor Lab is an experimental store that develops new flavors and tests consumer reactions. In the United States, it operates as a space showcasing limited menus and experimental products not sold at regular stores. Van Leeuwen has drawn attention by presenting original flavors that break the existing mold, including an espresso flavor developed in collaboration with Sabrina Carpenter, as well as mac and cheese and sunscreen flavors.The move is interpreted as a plan to cultivate Korea as a base for new product development, following its selection as the brand's first market in Asia. Kim Shin-young, executive vice president of A Twosome Place, which signed the master franchise (MF) agreement for the Korean entry, said, "We are preparing to introduce a store in Korea in the same form as the Flavor Lab in the United States." She added, "Since Van Leeuwen is a brand that deliciously creates fun and original flavors, we plan to gradually introduce new flavors in Korea as well."The industry views this as a result of the high assessment of the growth potential of Korea's premium ice cream market. Hanwha Galleria established its subsidiary Better Scoop Creamery and launched the premium ice cream brand "Benson" last year, expanding to 18 stores in about a year. Baekmidang, operated by Namyang Dairy Products, saw first-quarter sales this year reach 7.6 billion won after launching as an independent corporation last year, a 44% increase from the same period a year earlier. Operating profit also turned to a profit of 1.2 billion won in the first quarter this year, reversing a 300 million won loss in the first quarter of last year.Coffee brands are also growing premium ice cream into a key dessert offering. Terarosa developed and launched its own private brand (PB) ice cream using domestic raw milk and its own specialty coffee last year. After starting sales at 17 stores in the early stages of launch, it has now expanded operations to 26 stores on the back of customer response. Paul Bassett raised its seasonal product sales by about 30% from a year earlier by featuring lavender ice cream, which it relaunched at customer request, and presented limited flavors through a pop-up store at Shinsegae Department Store's Gangnam branch.#VanLeeuwen#IceCream#ATwosomePlace#PremiumDessert#KoreaFood#FlavorLab#FoodTrendOriginal reporting by Noh Hyun-young for Seoul Economic Daily.AI-translated from Korean.
